def-stiefel-grassmann-optimization-conve:
## Definition

For integers $1\le r\le n$, the **real Stiefel manifold** is
$$\operatorname{St}(n,r):=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}:X^{\mathsf T}X=I_r\}.$$
The **real Grassmannian** $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$ is the set of $r$-dimensional
linear subspaces of $\mathbb R^n$, identified with the quotient of
$\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ by the right action $X\mapsto XQ$ of
$\operatorname O(r)$. A frame $X$ represents the subspace
$[X]=\operatorname{range}(X)$.

On matrix spaces use the Frobenius inner product
$\langle U,V\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}V)$. Give Stiefel its
induced metric. On the Grassmann quotient use the quotient metric: identify a
tangent vector at $[X]$ with its unique horizontal representative $Z$ satisfying
$X^{\mathsf T}Z=0$, and pair horizontal representatives by the Frobenius inner
product. A Grassmann formula written with a frame representative must be
unchanged under $(X,Z)\mapsto(XQ,ZQ)$ for $Q\in\operatorname O(r)$.

For a matrix $M$, set $\operatorname{sym}(M)=(M+M^{\mathsf T})/2$.
def-complex-stiefel-grassmann-optimizati:
## Definition

For $1\le r\le n$, set $\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)=\{X\in\mathbb C^{n\times r}:X^*X=I_r\}$ and $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(r,n)=\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)/\operatorname U(r)$.
The class $[X]$ represents the complex column space of $X$; two orthonormal
frames represent the same space exactly when they differ by right multiplication
by a unitary $r\times r$ matrix. Regard each complex matrix space as a real
vector space and use the real Frobenius inner product
$$\langle U,V\rangle_{\mathbb R}:=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(U^*V).$$
Give the complex Stiefel manifold its induced metric. On the complex Grassmann
quotient, represent tangent vectors horizontally by matrices $Z$ with $X^*Z=0$
and pair these representatives by $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathbb R}$.
For $A=A_0+iA_1\in\mathbb C^{n\times r}$, write
$$\rho(A):=\begin{pmatrix}A_0&-A_1\\A_1&A_0\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{2n\times2r}$$
for its realification, the real matrix acting on real/imaginary coordinates as
$A$ acts on complex coordinates. Write $\operatorname{Herm}(A)=(A+A^*)/2$.
prop-stiefel-grassmann-are-compact:
## Statement

For $1\le r\le n$, $\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ is a nonempty closed bounded
subset of $\mathbb R^{n\times r}$, and $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$ is compact as
its continuous quotient image. Hence both spaces are compact.
prop-complex-stiefel-grassmann-are-compa:
## Statement

For $1\le r\le n$, $\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)$ is a nonempty closed
bounded subset of the real coordinate space $\mathbb R^{2nr}$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(r,n)$ is its continuous quotient image. Both
spaces are compact.
thm-stiefel-grassmann-tangent-projection:
## Statement

For $X\in\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, the tangent space and its Frobenius
orthogonal projection are
$$T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)=\{Z:X^{\mathsf T}Z+Z^{\mathsf T}X=0\},\qquad \Pi_X^{\rm St}(G)=G-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G).$$
For $[X]\in\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$, its tangent vectors have unique horizontal
representatives $Z$ with $X^{\mathsf T}Z=0$, and the quotient-metric projection
of an ambient $G$ to this horizontal space is
$$\Pi_X^{\rm Gr}(G)=(I-XX^{\mathsf T})G.$$
thm-complex-stiefel-grassmann-tangent-pr:
## Statement

For $X\in\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)$, as a real manifold, $T_X\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)=\{Z:X^*Z+Z^*X=0\}$ and $\Pi_X^{\rm St}(G)=G-X\operatorname{Herm}(X^*G)$. The complex Grassmann tangent has the unique horizontal representative $X^*Z=0$, and its quotient-metric projection is $\Pi_X^{\rm Gr}(G)=(I-XX^*)G$.
prop-stiefel-grassmann-riemannian-gradie:
## Statement

Let $F$ be smooth on an open neighborhood of $\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, and
write $G=\nabla F(X)$ for its Euclidean gradient. Its restriction to Stiefel
has Riemannian gradient $G-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G)$. If
$F(XQ)=F(X)$ for every $Q\in\operatorname O(r)$, it descends to a smooth
Grassmann objective and its gradient has horizontal representative
$(I-XX^{\mathsf T})G$. In either metric, gradient zero is equivalent to a
critical point of the restricted objective.
def-complex-grassmann-polar-retraction:
## Definition

For $X\in\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)$ and horizontal $\eta\in T_{[X]}\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(r,n)$, so $X^*\eta=0$, define $R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)=(X+\eta)\bigl((X+\eta)^*(X+\eta)\bigr)^{-1/2}$ and $R_{[X]}^{\rm pol}(\eta)=\operatorname{range}(R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta))$.
The inverse square root is the inverse of the unique positive-definite
Hermitian square root. The horizontal condition gives
$(X+\eta)^*(X+\eta)=I+\eta^*\eta\succ0$, so this map is defined for every
horizontal tangent vector, and its frame representative is unchanged as a
Grassmann point when $(X,\eta)$ is replaced by $(XQ,\eta Q)$ with unitary $Q$.
thm-complex-grassmann-polar-retraction-i:
## Statement

The frame formula of [[def-complex-grassmann-polar-retraction]] is smooth on the
horizontal tangent bundle, maps into $\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)$,
fixes zero, and has frame differential $D R_X^{\rm pol}(0)[\eta]=\eta$ for
horizontal $\eta$. It is right-unitary equivariant, so its range map is
representative-independent and has identity differential under the horizontal
tangent identification. Thus it is a first-order retraction on
$\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(r,n)$.
prop-complex-grassmann-projector-energy-:
## Statement

Let $1\le r\le n$, and let $E$ be real-valued and continuously differentiable on an open set of
Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices containing the rank-$r$ orthogonal projectors.
Suppose its real Frobenius gradient $K(P)=K(P)^*$ satisfies
$$DE(P)[H]=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(K(P)^*H)$$
for every Hermitian direction $H$. Then $f([X])=E(XX^*)$ is well-defined on
$\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(r,n)$ and has horizontal gradient
$$\operatorname{grad}f([X])=2(I-XX^*)K(XX^*)X.$$
def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions:
## Definition

For $X\in\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ and $\eta\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$,
put $Y=X+\eta$. On the domain where $Y$ has full column rank, let
$\operatorname{qf}(Y)$ be the $Q$ factor in the unique reduced QR factorization
$Y=QR$ with $R$ upper triangular and positive diagonal. Define the **QR map**
by $R_X^{\rm QR}(\eta)=\operatorname{qf}(X+\eta)$. Define the **polar map**
by
$$R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)=(X+\eta)\bigl((X+\eta)^{\mathsf T}(X+\eta)\bigr)^{-1/2},$$
where the exponent denotes the inverse of the unique positive-definite square
root. Both Stiefel maps induce Grassmann maps by taking the output column space.
The polar formula is right-equivariant:
$R_{XQ}^{\rm pol}(\eta Q)=R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)Q$ for every $Q\in\operatorname O(r)$.

These are defined only where the displayed input is full rank. In fact, for a
Stiefel tangent $\eta$, $X+\eta$ always has full column rank, since
$\|(X+\eta)v\|_2^2=\|v\|_2^2+\|\eta v\|_2^2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^r$.
thm-stiefel-retractions-are-first-order:
## Statement

On the full-column-rank domains of [[def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions]], the
positive-diagonal QR and polar maps are smooth, take values in
$\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, fix $\eta=0$, and have differential
$D R_X(0)[\eta]=\eta$. Their induced Grassmann maps are independent of the
representative and have identity differential under the horizontal tangent
identification. Thus they are first-order retractions. This theorem makes no
second-order claim; in particular, the QR map need not be second order.
alg-riemannian-armijo-backtracking:
## Definition

Let $M$ be $\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ or $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$, let $f:M\to\mathbb R$
be smooth, and choose one retraction $R$ from
[[def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions]]. At $x\in M$, let $g=\operatorname{grad}f(x)$.
Fix $a\in(0,1)$, $\beta\in(0,1)$ and an integer budget $J\ge0$.

If $g=0$, return `(x, stationary)`. Otherwise test, in order,
$t_j=\beta^j$ for $j=0,\ldots,J$. At each trial form $y_j=R_x(-t_jg)$;
if the chosen retraction's full-rank condition fails, reject that trial without
evaluating $f(y_j)$. Otherwise accept and return $(y_j,t_j)$ at the first index
with
$$f(y_j)\le f(x)-a t_j\|g\|^2.$$
If no trial passes, return `(x, budget-exhausted)`. The accepted update has
sufficient decrease; finite budget alone gives no success guarantee.
alg-riemannian-trust-region:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a real Stiefel manifold $\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, a real
Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$, or a complex Grassmannian
$\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(r,n)$, treating each tangent space as a real
inner-product space. Let $f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and choose a QR or polar
retraction $R$ from the corresponding real or complex definition. Fix
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $0<\gamma_{\rm dec}<1<\gamma_{\rm inc}$,
$0<\theta_C\le1$, a declared model-operator bound $M_B\ge0$, a maximum radius
$\Delta_{\max}>0$, an initial radius $0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{\max}$, target
$\varepsilon\ge0$, and finite outer cap $N\in\mathbb N_0$. Each self-adjoint
real-linear model operator $B_x$ on the Stiefel tangent or Grassmann horizontal space must
satisfy $\|B_x\|\le M_B$. The subproblem routine $S$ has a finite budget and
returns a candidate tangent vector or failure.

Starting at $x_0$, for $k=0,\ldots,N$ in order:

1. Set $g_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)$. Return (x_k, stationary) if
   $g_k=0$, (x_k, target-achieved) if $\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon$, and
   (x_k, outer-budget-exhausted) if $k=N$.
2. Form the pullback quadratic model
   $$m_k(s)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,B_{x_k}s\rangle.$$
   With $c_k=\langle g_k,B_{x_k}g_k\rangle$, set
   $$\tau_k=\begin{cases}\Delta_k/\|g_k\|,&c_k\le0,\\ \min\{\|g_k\|^2/c_k,\Delta_k/\|g_k\|\},&c_k>0,\end{cases} \qquad p_C=-\tau_k g_k.$$
   This is the coordinate-free negative-gradient segment minimizer of
   [[alg-trust-region-cauchy-step]]. Set
   $P_C=m_k(0)-m_k(p_C)>0$.
3. Query $S$. Use its candidate $q$ only if it returned a vector,
   $\|q\|\le\Delta_k$, and
   $m_k(0)-m_k(q)\ge\theta_C P_C$; otherwise use $p_C$. If
   $\Delta_k\le\|g_k\|/(2M_B)$, replace the candidate by $p_C$, interpreting
   that threshold as $+\infty$ when $M_B=0$. Set
   $P_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)$.
4. Form $y_k=R_{x_k}(p_k)$ and
   $\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(y_k))/P_k$. If the trial objective cannot be evaluated,
   return (x_k, model-evaluation-failure).
5. If $\rho_k<\eta_1$, reject and set
   $(x_{k+1},\Delta_{k+1})=(x_k,\gamma_{\rm dec}\Delta_k)$. Otherwise accept
   and set $x_{k+1}=y_k$. If also $\rho_k\ge\eta_2$ and $\|p_k\|=\Delta_k$,
   set $\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\gamma_{\rm inc}\Delta_k,\Delta_{\max}\}$; in every
   other accepted case set $\Delta_{k+1}=\Delta_k$.

Return the last accepted point with the corresponding stop status. A failed
finite subproblem call falls back to the Cauchy step; the outer cap remains a
possible stop and finite budget alone implies no convergence.
def-stiefel-grassmann-projected-vector-t:
## Definition

Let $X$ be a source frame, $\eta\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, and
$Z\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$. For Stiefel transport let $Y=R_X(\eta)$ be
either the QR or polar endpoint. For Grassmann transport specifically choose
$Y=R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)$, the polar endpoint; the positive-diagonal QR frame is
not used for this representative-based quotient transport. Define the
**projected Stiefel transport**
$$\mathcal T_Y^{\rm St}(Z):=Z-Y\operatorname{sym}(Y^{\mathsf T}Z),$$
and, for a horizontal source representative $Z$, define the **projected Grassmann transport representative**
$$\mathcal T_Y^{\rm Gr}(Z):=(I-YY^{\mathsf T})Z.$$
The Grassmann expression is interpreted as a tangent representative at
$[Y]$. The polar endpoint is right-equivariant, so the next proposition verifies
representative independence, tangency, and identity at a zero step. These
projection transports are not claimed to be Levi-Civita parallel transport.
lem-riemannian-trust-region-ratio-accura:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional real Stiefel or Grassmann manifold, or a
complex Grassmannian, with its real Frobenius metric. Regard every tangent
space as real, let $x\in M$, and let $g=\operatorname{grad}f(x)\ne0$.
Choose a first-order retraction $R$ and write
$\widehat f_x(s)=f(R_x(s))$ on the tangent (or horizontal) space. Suppose
$\nabla\widehat f_x$ is $L_R$-Lipschitz on the ball $\|s\|\le\Delta$, and let
$m_x(s)=f(x)+\langle g,s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,B_xs\rangle$ with
$B_x$ self-adjoint and $\|B_x\|\le M_B$. Let $p_C$ be the negative-gradient
Cauchy step, and let a feasible trial $p$ satisfy
$m_x(0)-m_x(p)\ge\theta_C[m_x(0)-m_x(p_C)]$ for $0<\theta_C\le1$.
With a zero denominator interpreted as $+\infty$, if
$\Delta\le\|g\|/(2M_B)$, then its predicted decrease $P$ is positive and
$$|\rho-1|\le\frac{2(L_R+M_B)\Delta}{\theta_C\|g\|},\qquad \rho=\frac{f(x)-f(R_x(p))}{P}.$$
Consequently, for $0<\eta_2<1$, if
$$\Delta\le \min\left\{\frac{\|g\|}{2M_B}, \frac{\theta_C(1-\eta_2)\|g\|}{2(L_R+M_B)}\right\},$$
then $\rho\ge\eta_2$. If $L_R+M_B=0$, the ratio equals $1$.
prop-stiefel-grassmann-vector-transport-:
## Statement

For every retraction step $\eta$ at $X$, the maps
[[def-stiefel-grassmann-projected-vector-transport]] are smooth linear maps in
the source tangent vector and take values in the endpoint tangent spaces; at
$\eta=0$ both return the input tangent
representative. The Grassmann map is representative-independent under
$(X,\eta,Z)\mapsto(XQ,\eta Q,ZQ)$.
thm-retraction-armijo-acceptance-and-ste:
## Statement

Let $M=\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ or $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$ be compact, let
$f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, and let $R$ be a QR or polar retraction with the
first-order property of [[thm-stiefel-retractions-are-first-order]]. Write
$\widehat f_x(\eta)=f(R_x(\eta))$. Assume a uniform bound
$\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\le G$ and a constant $L_R\ge0$ such that, for
every $x$ and $\|\eta\|\le1$,
$$\|\operatorname{grad}\widehat f_x(\eta)-\operatorname{grad}\widehat f_x(0)\|\le L_R\|\eta\|.$$
For $a\in(0,1)$ and a nonstationary iterate, set
$$\delta=\min\{1,(2G)^{-1},2(1-a)/L_R\},$$
where a reciprocal of zero is interpreted as $+\infty$. If the finite
backtracking budget tests some $t_j=\beta^j\le\delta$, then it accepts a step;
the first accepted step obeys $t\ge\beta\delta$. The bound
$t\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\le1/2$ keeps the pullback argument inside its
assumed unit tangent ball.
thm-retraction-armijo-best-iterate-compl:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[thm-retraction-armijo-acceptance-and-step-lower-bound]],
assume $f$ is bounded below by $f_{\inf}$ and every nonstationary call's finite
budget reaches the stated $\delta$. For $N\ge1$ accepted updates $x_0,\ldots,x_N$,
$$\min_{0\le k<N}\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\|^2 \le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{\inf}}{a\beta\delta N}.$$
In particular, after more than
$(f(x_0)-f_{\inf})/(a\beta\delta\epsilon^2)$ accepted updates, some iterate
among the pre-update points has gradient norm at most $\epsilon$. The order is
$O(\epsilon^{-2})$ with the displayed constants fixed. This counts accepted
updates; it does not assert an evaluation bound independent of the finite
backtracking budgets.
thm-riemannian-trust-region-first-order-:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a compact real Stiefel manifold or real Grassmannian, or a compact
complex Grassmannian, let $f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, and set
$f_{\inf}=\min_M f$. Assume the pullback
gradients of the chosen first-order retraction are uniformly $L_R$-Lipschitz
on every trial ball, and each self-adjoint real-linear model operator satisfies
$\|B_x\|\le M_B$. Run [[alg-riemannian-trust-region]] with fixed
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $0<\gamma_{\rm dec}<1<\gamma_{\rm inc}$,
$0<\theta_C\le1$, $0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{\max}$, and target
$0<\varepsilon\le1$. Assume every model and objective evaluation on a valid
trial is available. The counts concern the uncapped trial sequence up to its
first target iterate; for the finite-cap implementation, choose an outer cap
at least the resulting total-trial bound.

Using $+\infty$ for reciprocals of zero, define
$$c_\delta=\min\left\{\frac1{2M_B}, \frac{\theta_C(1-\eta_2)}{2(L_R+M_B)}\right\},\qquad c_R=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{\rm dec}\min\{c_\delta,\Delta_{\max}\}\},$$
$$c_P=\min\{c_R,1/M_B\},\qquad c_S=\tfrac12\eta_1\theta_Cc_P>0,\qquad r_\varepsilon=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{\rm dec}\min\{c_\delta\varepsilon,\Delta_{\max}\}\}.$$
Then the number $N_s$ of accepted steps and $N_u$ of rejected trials before
the first iterate with $\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon$ obey
$$N_s\le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{\inf}}{c_S\varepsilon^2},\qquad N_u\le \frac{\log(\Delta_0/r_\varepsilon)+N_s\log\gamma_{\rm inc}} {|\log\gamma_{\rm dec}|}.$$
Consequently accepted steps and total trials $N_s+N_u$ are
$O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, with all displayed
constants fixed. Such a finite cap suffices to return the target-achieved
status; a smaller cap may return outer-budget-exhausted first. The constants
and proof count accepted and rejected outer trials; they do not bound inner subproblem
operations.
